crrc-georgia-international-fellowship.about:
CRRC Georgia runs the Caucasus Barometer and many social-science research projects. International fellows work on research, interviewing, questionnaire design, outreach materials, databases and events, and can build long-term links with local researchers and policymakers.

The placement lasts at least 10 weeks, four days a week, in Tbilisi. Candidates with their own research agenda are prioritised.

CRRC encourages applicants to seek outside funding in addition to the small stipend and helps with finding housing.
crrc-georgia-international-fellowship.eligibility: Interest and background in the social sciences; at least two years of college completed when the internship starts (graduate students strongly encouraged); computer skills (SPSS/Stata a plus); able to commit at least 10 weeks. Russian or a regional language and NIS experience are a plus. No nationality restriction stated.
crrc-georgia-international-fellowship.costs: Small stipend; candidates are encouraged to find outside funding for travel and living costs.

eu-delegation-georgia-funded-traineeship.about:
The EU Delegation to Georgia offers funded traineeships to young graduates interested in international relations and the work of a diplomatic mission. The latest call placed a trainee in the Political, Press and Information Section: monitoring and reporting on Georgian developments, supporting events such as Europe Days, and drafting English and Georgian social media content.

Calls are managed directly by the Delegation, typically for a start in spring, summer or autumn, and each call names its section, deadline and exact requirements.

Trainees receive a monthly grant but pay their own travel, visa, insurance and accommodation.
eu-delegation-georgia-funded-traineeship.eligibility: Recent graduates with less than one year of professional experience after graduation; university degree in a relevant field (political science, law, IR, economics, communications). Very good English and Georgian (C1) for the latest call. Nationals of EU member states, pre-accession countries and the host country (Georgia) are generally eligible; confirm in each call.
eu-delegation-georgia-funded-traineeship.costs: Monthly grant paid by the Delegation; travel, visa, insurance and housing are not covered.

parliament-of-georgia-internship-program.about:
The Office of the Parliament of Georgia selects interns by open competition to work in structural units and committees, with the aim of supporting future careers and involving young people in public service. The programme began in 2004 with support from USAID and NDI.

Recent rounds last three months and are paid; interns present a report on a topic of interest at the end. Announcements and requirements are published on the Parliament's website for each round.

Note: the Parliament's website blocks automated access, so confirm the current round, pay and requirements on the page directly.
parliament-of-georgia-internship-program.eligibility: Students and graduates of Georgian higher education institutions; each announcement sets year-of-study and GPA requirements and Georgian-language skills. International applicants should check the announcement.

tbc-bank-internship-program-2027.about:
TBC Bank is Georgia's largest bank and runs a long-established paid internship for students and graduates. Interns choose one main area of interest (and optionally a second) such as retail and SME banking, finance, marketing, data and AI governance or investment banking, and work in hybrid or on-site teams depending on the department.

The 2026 round accepted applications from 28 September to 14 October, with a test on 18 October and interviews and assignments from 3 November to 3 December; interns start in January 2027. The programme lasts 6 to 12 months depending on progress and area, and TBC reports that most graduates continue their careers at the bank.

Questions go to the programme mailbox listed on the page. Check the page each September for the next call.
tbc-bank-internship-program-2027.eligibility: 2nd-year students of three-year programmes, 3rd and 4th-year bachelor's students, master's students and graduates. Georgian language and ability to work in Tbilisi are practically required; check the page for any work-permit rules for non-citizens.
tbc-bank-internship-program-2027.costs: Paid internship; no fee. Relocation to Tbilisi is the intern's own responsibility.

un-undp-georgia-internship-programme.about:
The UN in Georgia hosts interns through the UNDP Internship Programme at UN House in Tbilisi. Interns support programme teams with research, stakeholder databases, drafting and English-Georgian translation.

The internship is non-salaried: the student, nominating institution or government covers all costs including travel, visas, housing and insurance. Interns are not UN staff and the internship does not lead automatically to employment. UNDP's global policy has moved to stipends for some posts, so check the current vacancy notice for pay.

Applications are accepted year-round. You send a university enrolment letter, a reference from a senior faculty member, a short motivation paper and the internship application form to the programme focal point.
un-undp-georgia-internship-programme.eligibility: Enrolled in a graduate-level degree programme (typically 3rd or 4th year) in a development-related field such as economics, international relations or law, and returning to studies afterwards. Excellent English; Georgian and Russian are assets (local interns need strong English and Georgian). International applicants are accepted but must fund themselves.
un-undp-georgia-internship-programme.costs: Unpaid. Interns cover travel, visa, accommodation, subsistence and medical insurance.

adnoc-internship-programme.about:
ADNOC's internship programme places university students in Group companies across Abu Dhabi's energy sector. According to the official page it is open to UAE nationals and non-UAE nationals over 18, enrolled at selected universities and able to live in the UAE for the whole placement.

Undergraduates must have completed two years of full-time study (fourth-year students get priority). Minimum cumulative GPA is 2.8 for undergraduates and 3.0 for postgraduates. On-site placements require a medical fitness check and government approvals. Duration and pay are not stated on the page; confirm on the application portal.
adnoc-internship-programme.eligibility: UAE nationals or non-UAE nationals aged 18+, currently enrolled at one of ADNOC's selected universities; two years of full-time study completed; GPA 2.8 (undergraduate) / 3.0 (postgraduate); must be able to reside in the UAE during the placement; medical fitness and government approval for on-site roles.
how_to_apply: Open the ADNOC Internship Program page and check the list of partner universities.
Follow the link to the ADNOC jobs portal listing 'Developing-Internship'.
Create a profile and upload CV and transcript.
Attend assessments if shortlisted and complete the medical fitness check.
adnoc-internship-programme.costs: Pay and housing are not stated on the official page; check the portal listing.

aramco-university-internship-program.about:
The University Internship Program is Aramco's training scheme for students of Saudi universities and colleges. Placements last at least eight weeks, as required by the student's school, and depend on available slots.

The official page lists a monthly stipend, free housing (or a SAR 1,500 allowance if home or university is more than 80 km from the site), transportation and medical coverage. Registration opens only in announced windows; the latest page lists orientation on 17 January 2027 and start-up on 18 January 2027 for nominated applicants. Registration was closed when checked, so watch Aramco's announcements for the next window. NATIONALS ONLY: international students should look at Aramco Americas' separate summer student programme.
aramco-university-internship-program.eligibility: Saudi nationals only. Student at a Saudi university whose programme requires practical training; not yet graduated; not enrolled in classes during the placement; cumulative GPA at least 2.00/4 (technical majors) or 2.50/4 (non-technical).
how_to_apply: Wait for Aramco to announce the registration window.
Register and complete your profile at jobs.aramco.com.
Upload Saudi National ID, latest official transcript and a university letter stating purpose and length of training.
Await nomination and attend orientation.
aramco-university-internship-program.costs: Monthly stipend, housing or SAR 1,500 allowance, transportation and medical coverage per company policy. No fees.

bapco-energies-empower-internship.about:
Empower is Bapco Energies' annual summer internship, running July to August with results announced in June. It gives hands-on exposure across Bapco Refining, Upstream, Gas and other group companies in Bahrain.

The official page was not fully readable, so eligibility rules (particularly nationality) are unconfirmed; the group's other early-career schemes target Bahraini nationals, so treat this as probably nationals-focused and check the page.
bapco-energies-empower-internship.eligibility: University student; nationality rules not confirmed (probably Bahraini nationals) - check the official page.
how_to_apply: Open the Empower Internship page on the Bapco Energies site.
Complete the online application when the window opens (spring).
Await results in June.

blackrock-summer-internship-emea-2027.about:
BlackRock's EMEA Summer Internship Program places penultimate-year students in investments, client and product, and corporate functions. You may apply to only one programme and up to two functions.

After submitting, you complete a pre-interview assessment that must be finished in the set window; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
blackrock-summer-internship-emea-2027.eligibility: Candidates in the penultimate year of an undergraduate or master's degree, graduating in 2028; local language fluency is required for Continental Europe offices. Right to work in the chosen country.
how_to_apply: Pick your office on the BlackRock careers site.
Submit the online application and CV.
Complete the pre-interview recorded assessment within the window.
Interview with the chosen functions.

dp-world-forsa-internship.about:
Forsa is part of DP World's Emiratisation initiative and gives university students practical experience across the group. Participants receive a certificate of practical experience endorsed by DP World management.

NATIONALS ONLY: DP World's student pages sit under its UAE Emiratisation section; applicants need a Family Book and a university letter specifying the internship period. Expats should check DP World's global graduate pages instead.
dp-world-forsa-internship.eligibility: UAE nationals only (Family Book), enrolled at a university; university letter stating the requested internship period.
how_to_apply: Open the Forsa page on DP World's UAE careers site.
Click Apply now and register.
Upload Family Book and university letter.
Wait for placement confirmation.
dp-world-forsa-internship.costs: Pay not stated on pages reviewed.

ega-summer-internship-uae-nationals.about:
EGA hosts UAE national students each summer for hands-on placements in its aluminium operations, chiefly in STEM fields; past cohorts included high-school students.

NATIONALS ONLY: a valid UAE passport is required and only completed online applications are reviewed.
ega-summer-internship-uae-nationals.eligibility: UAE nationals with a valid UAE passport; complete online application.
how_to_apply: Open EGA's student opportunities page.
Complete the online application in full.
Await shortlisting.

emirates-group-elevate-internship-2027.about:
Elevate is the Emirates Group's internship scheme for final-year Bachelor's/Master's students and recent graduates, run full-time in Dubai for six months. The 2027 cohort (start 11 January 2027) closed applications on 28 September 2026; the programme recurs yearly, so expect the next round to open around mid-2027.

Secondary sources report that candidates need prior internship experience and must not have interned at the Group before; check conditions and nationality rules on the Emirates Group careers portal, as third-party reports conflict. Applications are submitted online only.
emirates-group-elevate-internship-2027.eligibility: Final-year Bachelor's/Master's student or recent graduate, available full-time in Dubai for six months, reportedly with at least one prior internship. Check the current nationality/visa terms on the careers portal (reports conflict on whether all nationalities qualify).
how_to_apply: Watch the Emirates Group careers portal for the next Elevate round.
Create a profile and submit the online application with CV and transcripts.
Complete online assessments and interviews if shortlisted.
Prepare visa and start date (January cohorts).
emirates-group-elevate-internship-2027.costs: Paid internship; amount not confirmed on official pages. No application fee.

emirates-group-take-off-internship.about:
Take-Off is the Emirates Group's internship track for UAE national students at universities in the UAE and abroad. Length follows the student's internship requirement and can run up to 12 months.

NATIONALS ONLY: this record is included so that residents and expats know the route exists but is not open to them; they should look at the Elevate internship instead. Details were confirmed from careers-portal listings; check the portal for the current round.
emirates-group-take-off-internship.eligibility: UAE nationals only, enrolled at a university and needing practical training.
how_to_apply: Check the Emirates Group careers portal for the Take-Off listing.
Apply online with CV and university letter.
Attend interview if shortlisted.
emirates-group-take-off-internship.costs: Pay terms not published on pages reviewed.

isdb-internship-program.about:
The IsDB Internship Program offers short placements in IsDB business units at headquarters in Jeddah or in one of its 10 Regional Hubs and Centres of Excellence. Interns must not exceed a cumulative 6 months of internship at IsDB.

Openings are advertised on the IsDB careers site, where candidates apply to the specific posting.
isdb-internship-program.eligibility: Enrolled as an undergraduate or graduate student, or graduated within the last year. Age 30 or younger by the deadline. Cumulative GPA of at least 3.5/4.0 or equivalent; current students need an official request or recommendation from their university. Applicants should come from top universities worldwide or in member countries and must be legally authorised to stay in the country of the host unit. No nationality restriction is stated.
how_to_apply: Open careers.isdb.org and the Internship Program page
Check current internship postings under Current Opportunities
Apply online to the posting with CV and university request letter
Check IsDB's note that it charges no recruitment fees
isdb-internship-program.costs: The page does not state a stipend. IsDB states it never charges fees during recruitment.

isdb-young-professionals-program.about:
The YPP is a 24-month programme with job rotations, a two-year training curriculum and mentoring, based at IsDB headquarters in Jeddah with rotations to Regional Hubs and country missions.

Applications run in January-February, followed by screening, technical review, interviews and assessments; the cohort starts in September or October and the start date is not flexible.
isdb-young-professionals-program.eligibility: Master's degree in a relevant field from a reputable university, completed within four years before the deadline; up to five years of relevant experience (none required). Age 32 or under at the deadline (extended by mandatory military service). Priority goes to citizens of IsDB member countries, but non-member nationals may also apply. Excellent English.
how_to_apply: Watch careers.isdb.org for the January-February application window
Apply online under Current Opportunities
Complete assessments and interviews at IsDB headquarters (May/June)
Sign the contract and start in September or October
isdb-young-professionals-program.costs: Internationally competitive tax-free salary plus medical coverage, annual tickets, education allowance and retirement plan; figures are not published on the page. Contact: ypp@isdb.org.

masdar-summer-internship.about:
Masdar posts summer internships each year on its SmartRecruiters page, in departments such as Environment, Sustainability & Risk. The 2026 posting asked for 3rd/4th-year undergraduates studying in the UAE, or studying abroad with a valid UAE visa, a cumulative GPA of 3.0+, and a relevant major; it ran June to August 2026.

No nationality restriction appeared in the posting, making it one of the more accessible routes for UAE-based international students. Postings for the next summer typically appear in early spring; roles and requirements differ by department.
masdar-summer-internship.eligibility: 3rd or 4th-year undergraduate currently studying in the UAE (or abroad with a valid UAE visa); GPA 3.0+; major relevant to the department. Posting listed no nationality limit; check each role.
how_to_apply: Watch the Masdar page on SmartRecruiters for 'Summer Internship 2027' postings.
Apply to the department matching your major.
Provide CV, transcript and GPA.
Interview and, if selected, prepare a UAE visa.
masdar-summer-internship.costs: Pay not stated in the posting summary; check the role.

misk-foundation-internship-program.about:
Misk's skills programmes (internships, traineeships, global and remote placements) are listed on the Misk Hub, where applicants create a profile, apply and, for some programmes, interview. The listings seen mostly require Saudi nationality and English and Arabic fluency.

NATIONALS ONLY probably: included for completeness. Details for this specific listing were not opened; confirm on the page.
misk-foundation-internship-program.eligibility: Probably Saudi nationals; check the listing for age, education and language requirements.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on hub.misk.org.sa.
Open the internship listing and apply.
Complete evaluation and interview.

qapco-internship-program.about:
QAPCO, the petrochemical producer in Mesaieed, offers internships for students at Qatar universities as part of its Qatarization work, with priority for partner universities.

The page is part of the Qatarization section, so eligibility may favour Qatari nationals; terms, length and pay were not visible in the sources checked. Confirm on the page.
qapco-internship-program.eligibility: Students at universities in Qatar (partner universities prioritised); nationality terms unconfirmed, likely Qatari nationals first.
how_to_apply: Open the QAPCO Qatarization internship page.
Follow the application instructions.
Provide university letter and transcript.

qatar-airways-al-darb-summer-internship.about:
Qatar Airways' Al Darb Qatarisation programme includes a summer internship for national university students (about 40 to 60 interns a year). Each intern is paired with a coach and receives a salary; some universities grant course credit.

NATIONALS ONLY: included so non-Qataris know it is closed to them. Dates are not published on the page reviewed.
qatar-airways-al-darb-summer-internship.eligibility: Qatari national university students; successful interview with Qatar Airways.
how_to_apply: Open the Qatar Airways Qatarisation internship page.
Apply when the summer intake is announced.
Attend an interview.

qatarenergy-lng-internship-program-2027.about:
QatarEnergy LNG runs an annual summer internship of 4 to 8 weeks for undergraduates. The 2026 cycle ran 7 June to 27 August with a 31 March deadline; the next cycle is expected on a similar calendar.

The careers listing reads 'national and non-national (children of employees)' undergraduates, so non-Qataris are accepted only as children of employees; high-school places were reserved for Qataris. Questions go to the company's internship mailbox.
qatarenergy-lng-internship-program-2027.eligibility: Qatari nationals enrolled in an undergraduate degree; non-nationals only if they are children of QatarEnergy LNG employees. High-school places for Qataris only.
how_to_apply: Wait for the careers site to reopen applications (around Q1 2027).
Create a user account and agree to the terms.
Submit a complete application; incomplete ones are rejected.
Selected applicants are emailed after screening.
qatarenergy-lng-internship-program-2027.costs: Pay not stated; ignore anyone asking for fees.

sidra-medicine-medical-observership.about:
The Observership lets visitors observe clinical work in areas such as paediatrics and subspecialties, women's services (OB/GYN), neonatology, surgery and diagnostics. It is observation only and does not lead to clinical privileges, licensure or employment.

Open to physicians, residents and fellows, medical students, high-school students, and nurses and allied health professionals; international applicants may also be considered. Length ranges from a few days to several weeks, set by Sidra.

Observers are unpaid, may be charged fees depending on duration and placement type, and must cover their own travel, accommodation, visa and insurance.
sidra-medicine-medical-observership.eligibility: Physicians, residents/fellows, medical students, high-school students, nurses and allied health professionals. International applicants may be considered. Subject to department approval and onboarding requirements.
how_to_apply: Email medicalobservership@sidra.org with the subject line 'Medical Observership Application'
Complete the administrative and onboarding requirements before the start date
sidra-medicine-medical-observership.costs: Unpaid. Fees may apply depending on duration, department and placement type; travel, housing, visa and insurance are the applicant's responsibility.

wcmq-specialized-biomedical-research-tra.about:
SBRT places recent bachelor's or master's graduates in a WCM-Q research group for at least six and at most twelve continuous months. Candidates at other career stages are considered case by case.

Applicants must find their own host: contact a WCM-Q research faculty member in your field first, then apply online with a letter of support from that faculty host naming the project and duration. Faculty approval does not guarantee a place.

The page does not say whether the placement is paid.
wcmq-specialized-biomedical-research-tra.eligibility: Qatari nationals and long-term residents of Qatar; recent bachelor's or master's graduates of universities in Qatar are welcome; other career stages case by case.
how_to_apply: Contact a WCM-Q research faculty member in your field and agree a project
Submit the online application: CV, passport copy, ID copy, latest transcript, one recommendation
Include the faculty host's supporting letter naming the project and duration
Questions: brtp@qatar-med.cornell.edu
wcmq-specialized-biomedical-research-tra.costs: Stipend not stated on the page.

chevening-scholarships-2027-28.about:
Chevening Scholarships are fully funded one-year master's awards at UK universities for outstanding emerging leaders, with no upper age limit. Awards are given through country-specific rounds; Georgia appears among the countries on the official site, while Qatar was not listed on the scholarships overview page, so check the country selector.

The 2027/28 round opened in August 2026 and closed in October 2026 (closing time 11:00 UTC on the date set for each country). Studies begin in September or October 2027. Applicants must meet the work-experience and eligibility rules published on the site and return to their home country for at least two years after the award.

The next round is expected to follow the same August to October pattern in 2027.
chevening-scholarships-2027-28.eligibility: Citizens of Chevening-eligible countries (check the country selector on the official site; Georgia is listed). Applicants need an undergraduate degree, the required work experience, and must meet the English and return-home requirements in the official guide.
how_to_apply: Select your country and award type on the official site
Check the eligibility guide and work-experience rules
Apply online in the August to October window
Choose up to three UK courses and submit references
Interview if shortlisted
chevening-scholarships-2027-28.costs: Covers tuition, a monthly stipend, travel and visa costs and other allowances.

jasso-honors-scholarship-privately-finan.about:
The Honors Scholarship pays 48,000 yen per month (30,000 yen for Japanese language institutions), usually for one year (April to March) or six months (October to March). It is for privately financed international students with excellent results and financial need, who hold the Student residence status.

Before coming to Japan, take the EJU with the Apply for Reservation Program box selected and enrol as a regular student; after arrival, contact your school. Typical requirements: previous-year GPA of at least 2.30, JLPT N2, EJU Japanese 200 or CEFR B2 English, and household income limits. Schools have limited slots.
jasso-honors-scholarship-privately-finan.eligibility: Privately financed international students (not Dependent or Long-term Resident status) at eligible Japanese institutions; excellent grades, financial need, and language level as listed. No nationality restriction stated, so students from Georgia and Qatar can apply.
how_to_apply: Register for the EJU and choose the Reservation Program, or contact your Japanese school after enrolment
Meet GPA and language thresholds
Submit documents to your school's international office
jasso-honors-scholarship-privately-finan.costs: 48,000 yen per month (30,000 yen for language institutions).

jasso-student-exchange-support-2027.about:
The Student Exchange Support Program pays 80,000 yen per month for 8 days to 1 year to students from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan who are accepted by a Japanese host school under a short-term exchange agreement.

Students must have excellent academic performance, need financial support, be able to obtain Student status of residence (not needed for 90 days or less), and return to their home institution to graduate. Total monthly scholarships from other sources must not exceed 80,000 yen.
jasso-student-exchange-support-2027.eligibility: University students from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwan and Palestine also eligible) whose home university has an exchange agreement with a Japanese school; includes Georgia and Qatar if the agreement exists.
how_to_apply: Ask your home university's international office whether it has an agreement with a Japanese school
Get nominated and accepted by the host school
Apply for the JASSO award through the university

russian-government-scholarship-quota-202.about:
The official website for the selection of foreign citizens to study in Russia handles the Russian Government scholarship quota, which covers bachelor's, master's and doctoral levels. Details of eligibility, benefits and the application dates are on the portal.

The quota typically includes free tuition, a monthly stipend and dormitory place, and often a preparatory language year; confirm the current terms on the portal before applying. Applicants normally apply online and choose up to several universities, then take part in a selection run through the local Russian representation.
russian-government-scholarship-quota-202.eligibility: Foreign citizens; quota places are allocated per country via the portal. Check the portal for Georgia and Qatar quota availability, as these were not confirmed on the fetched page.
how_to_apply: Register on the official portal
Choose study level and universities
Upload documents and submit
Await selection and invitation
russian-government-scholarship-quota-202.costs: Tuition covered; stipend and dormitory typically included (confirm on portal).

adb-internship-program.about:
ADB places graduate students in its departments for work related to their studies, such as economics, infrastructure, climate and finance. Assignments are posted at ADB.org with their own deadlines, and students do not need a nomination from their university.

Interns receive a stipend, but must cover accommodation, food, transport and part of the airfare, and buy comprehensive insurance before travel.
adb-internship-program.eligibility: National of an ADB member country with excellent English; enrolled in a master's or PhD programme at a school in an ADB member country for the whole internship; studies relevant to ADB work (2-3 years of experience preferred). Undergraduates, past interns and relatives of ADB staff cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Sign up for ADB job alerts and watch the internship page for open assignments.
Apply online through the ADB recruitment system before the posted deadline.
Provide proof of enrolment and your CV.
If selected (usually March-April for June starts), arrange insurance and travel.
adb-internship-program.costs: Stipend paid; accommodation, food, transport and part of airfare are the intern's responsibility.

african-union-internship-programme.about:
The African Union Internship Programme places students and graduates in AU units for at least three months, with a possible three-month extension depending on performance and the host unit. The schedule is full-time, Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 17:00.

The page states that the AU provides no financial support: no living expenses, no travel reimbursement and no per diem, and no sick leave. Interns arrange their own travel, lodging and living costs.
african-union-internship-programme.eligibility: Nationals of an AU Member State, aged 22 to 32 at application; full-time students in the final year of undergraduate or postgraduate study, or graduates of a recognised institution; fluency in one AU working language (Arabic, English, French, Portuguese or Kiswahili). Citizens of Georgia and Qatar are not eligible, as they are not AU Member State nationals.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on the AU Careers portal
Upload motivation letter, passport or national ID copy, certified academic certificates, CV and an institutional recommendation letter
Submit and watch for the confirmation email
Track your status on the portal
african-union-internship-programme.costs: Unpaid. No stipend, travel, accommodation or living-expense support; interns cover all costs.

aiib-global-internship-program.about:
AIIB's Global Internship Program places graduate students in its Beijing headquarters (research internships can also be remote or in person). It is one of three AIIB Young Talent Programs, alongside the Graduate Program and the Legal Associate Program.

The annual selection starts in late December, with selection in March, offers in April and a start in May or June. Applicants complete an online application followed by a short chat-based screening.

Interns are paid in US dollars (USD 90 per workday on the 2026 page) and receive a roundtrip flight to Beijing.
aiib-global-internship-program.eligibility: Open to candidates of any citizenship (the page states no nationality requirement). Must be enrolled full-time in a master's or doctoral programme and plan to return to school, or have graduated in the same year as applying (the FAQ says graduates and non-diploma students are not eligible, so confirm on the page). Excellent academic record and fluent written and spoken English. Degrees aligned with AIIB's goals (economics, finance, social science, environment) preferred. Internships are full-time only.
how_to_apply: Open the AIIB Global Internship Program page and check the current year's intake
Submit the online application during the window that opens in late December
Complete the short chat-based screening
Wait for selection (March) and offers (April)
aiib-global-internship-program.costs: Paid: USD 90 per workday on the 2026 page plus a roundtrip flight to Beijing; interns arrange their own accommodation. No application fee is mentioned.

airbus-internships.about:
Airbus offers university students internships typically lasting three months to a year, hosted in France, Germany (internships and working-student roles), Spain (Getafe, Sevilla, Albacete, Illescas, Cádiz), the UK (Industry Placement, paid), the US and a Finland trainee programme in Jyväskylä and Helsinki.

You must be enrolled at a university; in France, Germany and the UK you must stay enrolled for the whole contract. Interns may receive financial compensation depending on length and national policy, plus paid leave.

Apply online only via the Airbus job board with a candidate account: CV, cover letter, certificates and grades (German applicants add a certificate of enrolment). Selected candidates have an interview or assessment centre.
airbus-internships.eligibility: Enrolled university students; must remain enrolled throughout in France, Germany and the UK; work-permit rules depend on the country of the placement (not stated on the page).
how_to_apply: Open the Airbus internships page and choose your country
Create a candidate account on the Airbus job board
Upload CV, cover letter, certificates and grades
Attend the interview or assessment centre
airbus-internships.costs: Compensation varies by country and duration; UK placements are paid. Amounts not published on the page.

airbus-pupil-internships-germany.about:
The Airbus internships page names 'Germany: pupil internships' as a separate programme with its own criteria, alongside university internships and the Finland trainee scheme. The central page does not give duration, age or pay; these are on the Germany pupil-internship page.

Applications are online only through the Airbus job board with a candidate account. Typical pupil work experience is short and unpaid, but confirm on the country page.
airbus-pupil-internships-germany.eligibility: School pupils; criteria are on the Airbus Germany pupil-internship page. German-language ability is likely needed; not stated on the central page.
how_to_apply: Open the Airbus internships page and choose Germany: pupil internships
Create a candidate account on the Airbus job board
Apply with CV and cover letter
airbus-pupil-internships-germany.costs: Pay not stated; school work experience is typically unpaid.

amazon-sde-internship-2027.about:
Amazon's SDE internships target students and graduates and require strong coding, data structures, algorithms and object-oriented design. Selection includes an online assessment followed by virtual interviews, with a reply within about five business days after interviews.

The official page says internships are for rising seniors and recent graduates; your offer states location and start date. Amazon hires interns at locations around the world.
amazon-sde-internship-2027.eligibility: Rising seniors and recent graduates with an undergraduate, master's or doctoral degree (per Amazon's internships page). Work authorisation depends on the country of the posting.
how_to_apply: Find SDE intern roles on amazon.jobs
Submit CV
Take the online coding assessment
Complete virtual interviews
amazon-sde-internship-2027.costs: Paid; pay is stated on each posting and varies by country.

anu-future-research-talent-awards-india.about:
The Future Research Talent (FRT) Awards are offered jointly by three ANU colleges and let high-achieving students from India spend 11-12 weeks on a collaborative research project with an ANU research school. Suggested timing: May to July (negotiable with the host group). Some projects can be extended with extra funding.

Awardees receive AUD 8,500 to cover return airfare, visa and medical costs, insurance, accommodation and living expenses; they manage the funds themselves and must spend them within 12 months. Selection weighs academic merit, research experience, the ANU host school's ranking and the ranking of the India home institution.

This is an institution-nominated scheme: your university must be on the collaborating-institution list (a PDF on the page), and it runs the first selection round.
anu-future-research-talent-awards-india.eligibility: Citizens of India residing in India, enrolled in a programme with a research component at a collaborating India institution and nominated by it. Not for citizens of other countries (including Georgia and Qatar). Previous FRT recipients are ineligible. In exceptional cases a Dean may approve students of non-partner institutions.
how_to_apply: Check with your institution's international/collaboration office that it is on the 2027 collaborating-institution list
The institution runs the first selection and nominates students; ANU makes the final choice
If your institution is not listed, email frt.science@anu.edu.au
Watch for the next round (applications closed 25 Sep 2026 for 2027)
anu-future-research-talent-awards-india.costs: Award of AUD 8,500 covers airfare, visa, insurance, accommodation and living expenses; no application fee stated.

anu-future-research-talent-awards-indone.about:
The Future Research Talent (FRT) Awards are offered jointly by three ANU colleges and let high-achieving students from Indonesia spend 11-12 weeks on a collaborative research project with an ANU research school. Suggested timing: June to September (negotiable with the host group). Some projects can be extended with extra funding.

Awardees receive AUD 8,500 to cover return airfare, visa and medical costs, insurance, accommodation and living expenses; they manage the funds themselves and must spend them within 12 months. Selection weighs academic merit, research experience, the ANU host school's ranking and the ranking of the Indonesia home institution.

This is an institution-nominated scheme: your university must be on the collaborating-institution list (a PDF on the page), and it runs the first selection round.
anu-future-research-talent-awards-indone.eligibility: Citizens of Indonesia residing in Indonesia, enrolled in a programme with a research component at a collaborating Indonesia institution and nominated by it. Not for citizens of other countries (including Georgia and Qatar). Previous FRT recipients are ineligible. In exceptional cases a Dean may approve students of non-partner institutions.
how_to_apply: Check with your institution's international/collaboration office that it is on the 2027 collaborating-institution list
The institution runs the first selection and nominates students; ANU makes the final choice
If your institution is not listed, email frt.science@anu.edu.au
Watch for the next round (applications closed 25 Sep 2026 for 2027)
anu-future-research-talent-awards-indone.costs: Award of AUD 8,500 covers airfare, visa, insurance, accommodation and living expenses; no application fee stated.

asse-international-student-exchange.about:
On the ASSE site the pitch is a school year abroad living with a host family and returning with cultural understanding and lasting friendships. The public page lists the partner-office countries but does not publish ages, fees or scholarships; those depend on the partner office in your own country and come with a downloadable brochure.

Because the organiser works through national partner offices, treat this as the starting point: pick the office for your country, then check price, deadlines and scholarship options there.
asse-international-student-exchange.eligibility: High-school students; age, language and country availability depend on the ASSE partner office in your country.
how_to_apply: Open asse.com and find the partner office for your country.
Download the brochure and request price, deadlines and scholarship information.
Apply through the partner office.
asse-international-student-exchange.costs: Not published on the public page; ask your partner office.

bain-associate-consultant-internship.about:
Students with one full summer left before graduation can apply, from any field of study. Interns start with intensive training and join a live case team; strong performers can get a full-time offer.

Bain has local variants, such as the Nordics ACI (for third-year bachelor's or first-year master's students) and the Korea Associate Consultant Trainee.
bain-associate-consultant-internship.eligibility: Current students with one summer left before graduation (graduating by June 2028 for the current cycle at some offices); any major. Right to work in the chosen office.
how_to_apply: Pick your office or campus page.
Submit CV (Word or PDF) and application on the Bain recruiting portal.
Online tests and case interviews.
Offer.

bank-of-england-summer-internship-2027.about:
The Bank of England runs a 10-week summer internship for university students across its Future Talent programmes. Interns join real teams working on monetary policy, financial stability, markets or technology.

The Bank also offers a Black Heritage Sponsored Internship for penultimate-year students of Black heritage, with at least GBP 5,000 funding for living costs for a year.
bank-of-england-summer-internship-2027.eligibility: University students (check the advert for year of study). Applicants must normally have the right to work in the UK for the internship; the page does not describe visa sponsorship, so confirm in the advert. English required.
how_to_apply: Register on the Bank of England Future Talent page to be reminded when applications open (November 2026).
Choose the internship area and submit CV and application.
Complete the online assessments.
Attend interviews and assessment.

banque-de-france-internships.about:
Banque de France internships are mainly for students in their final year (bac+4/5) or on a gap year (année de césure) and are covered by an internship agreement with the school. You respond to an online offer on the recruitment portal, and if your profile matches you are interviewed by the manager.

The recruitment pages are in French.
banque-de-france-internships.eligibility: Mainly students in the final year (bac+4/5) or on a gap year; a signed internship agreement (convention de stage) with your school is required. Nationality is not mentioned on the page; non-EU students should check visa rules for France. French is probably needed as the pages are in French.
how_to_apply: Browse offers on the Banque de France candidate portal (Workday)
Apply to a matching internship offer
Interview with the manager
Sign the internship agreement with your school
banque-de-france-internships.costs: Pay (gratification) is not stated on the page.

bcg-nordics-visiting-associate-internshi.about: The Visiting Associate Internship lets university students in years two to four of their studies join BCG teams in the Nordics, with applications reviewed year-round.
bcg-nordics-visiting-associate-internshi.eligibility: University students in years 2-4; check the page for work-permit and language requirements.
how_to_apply: Open the Nordics page and choose the office.
Submit CV and transcript.
Online assessment.
Case interviews.

bcg-uk-summer-internship-2027.about:
Interns work on client cases with BCG teams. Applicants upload a CV and then complete a short numerical assessment before interviews.

BCG recruits for summer internships in many other offices (Italy in January, Latin America in November, Korea, Nordics year-round).
bcg-uk-summer-internship-2027.eligibility: Penultimate-year undergraduate or master's students; right to work in the UK; fluent English.
how_to_apply: Apply online between 1 and 24 January 2027.
Upload CV and complete numerical assessment.
Case interviews.
Offer.

bis-graduate-programme.about:
The BIS Graduate Programme is a contract of up to 11 months at the headquarters in Basel in areas such as monetary policy, economics, financial stability, banking, risk management, technology, cyber-security and data science.

Positions are usually advertised in spring under current vacancies on bis.org.
bis-graduate-programme.eligibility: Recent or soon-to-be graduates with a bachelor's or master's degree, strong analytical skills, relevant interests and excellent English. Open to candidates of all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Check bis.org current vacancies (usually in spring)
Apply to the Graduate Programme posting online
Follow the BIS selection steps
bis-graduate-programme.costs: Salary net of Swiss income tax, health insurance, return travel and accommodation in Basel; the amount is not published on the page.

bis-phd-fellowship-programme.about:
PhD fellows work in the Monetary and Economic Department on topics such as financial intermediation and regulation, financial innovation and digitisation, monetary policy, fiscal policy and international finance.

The positions are posted at bis.org/careers under current vacancies in summer and autumn.
bis-phd-fellowship-programme.eligibility: Current PhD students in economics, finance or a related field with strong knowledge of financial and monetary economics, research experience and the ability to apply economic analysis tools. Open to candidates of all nationalities, located anywhere in the world.
how_to_apply: Watch bis.org current vacancies in summer and autumn
Apply online to the PhD Fellowship posting
Complete selection steps
bis-phd-fellowship-programme.costs: Competitive salary, health insurance, travel and relocation assistance including accommodation; amounts not published on the page.

blackrock-off-cycle-internship-emea-2027.about: BlackRock lists an off-cycle internship for EMEA alongside the main summer programme; applicants complete a pre-interview assessment.
blackrock-off-cycle-internship-emea-2027.eligibility: Students; check posting for graduation year and right to work.
how_to_apply: Open posting.
Apply online.
Pre-interview assessment.
Interviews.

bloomberg-news-internship-2027.about:
Bloomberg News posts Summer 2027 internships for roles such as data reporter, digital editor, video journalist and graphics. Postings exist in the US, the Netherlands, South Africa and Japan, each with own language and timing rules.

Apply with a CV and cover letter through Bloomberg's careers portal. Verify location, language requirement and deadline on each posting.
bloomberg-news-internship-2027.eligibility: Current university students or recent graduates; roles can require local language (e.g. Dutch for Amsterdam). Work authorisation for the posting's country is required.
how_to_apply: Open the Bloomberg careers portal
Filter for News internships 2027
Submit CV and cover letter for the role and city

bofa-student-leaders-2027.about:
Student Leaders places college students in paid internships with local nonprofits in Bank of America markets, plus a required three-day Summit in Charlotte in June 2027 (travel and lodging for the summit are covered).

The programme used to target high school students; for 2027 it is for students entering their second year of college. You must be 18+, earned a diploma within the last 24 months, hold a 3.0 GPA, have a recent leadership role, be legally authorised to work in the US without sponsorship through July 2027, and live in an eligible market during the summer.

Pay is USD 18 per hour (or higher local minimum), minimum 35 hours a week; housing and commuting are not covered.
bofa-student-leaders-2027.eligibility: US-based: 18+, high-school diploma within 24 months, entering second year of college in 2027-28, GPA 3.0+, leadership role, legally authorised to work in the US without sponsorship through July 2027, living in an eligible market. Not open to students needing visa sponsorship.
how_to_apply: Check eligible markets on the Bank of America site
Apply online between 14 Dec 2026 and 15 Feb 2027
Submit transcript and leadership details
Wait for decisions by 15 Apr 2027
bofa-student-leaders-2027.costs: Paid USD 18/hour or local minimum wage; summit travel, lodging and meals covered; housing and commuting not covered.

brookings-internship-program.about:
Brookings offers paid internships to nearly 150 degree-seeking students each year, and occasionally recent graduates, in its five research programmes and in communications, finance, HR and other units. Cohorts run in spring, summer and fall; for spring 2027 openings were posted from the week of 5 October, applications closed 7 November 2026 and selections are made 18 December.

Openings are posted on the Brookings iCIMS internship board; the Internship Program Details PDF has timelines and expectations.
brookings-internship-program.eligibility: Degree-seeking students, and occasionally recent graduates. The page does not state whether international students or those needing US work authorization are eligible, so confirm in the posting or with Brookings before applying; most non-US students would need valid US work authorisation (for example F-1 CPT/OPT).
how_to_apply: Watch the Brookings internship page for the next cohort's openings
Apply through the iCIMS internship job board
Read the Internship Program Details PDF
brookings-internship-program.costs: Paid; rate not stated on the page.

bundesbank-university-internships.about:
The Bundesbank offers internships so that students see what a central bank does in practice, including its core tasks and cross-functional support. Each student may complete at most two Bundesbank internships, one per study stage (first bachelor's; later after a bachelor's degree).

Apply through the online form linked at the end of the job advertisement on the Bundesbank job portal; state the desired period in the cover letter and include your study regulations if the internship is mandatory.
bundesbank-university-internships.eligibility: University students (bachelor's up to 3 months, master's/doctorate up to 6 months). Maximum two Bundesbank internships, one per study stage. No nationality requirement is stated; if your internship needs a visa, check the German Federal Foreign Office visa navigator. The page is in German, so German skills are likely needed.
how_to_apply: Find an advertised internship on jobportal.bundesbank.de
Apply via the online form at the end of the advertisement
Give your desired period in the cover letter and attach complete documents
Apply at least 4 months before the start date
bundesbank-university-internships.costs: Gross pay on a full-time basis: EUR 1,200 per month without a bachelor's degree, EUR 2,400 with one.

carnegie-endowment-internships.about:
Carnegie offers several internships across its research network, in Washington, DC and at Carnegie Europe, Carnegie China, Carnegie India and the Malcolm H. Kerr Carnegie Middle East Center, each with its own information page.

All interns, part-time or full-time, earn at least USD 20 per hour; full-time interns receive a benefits package. Browse openings on the Carnegie applicant portal.
carnegie-endowment-internships.eligibility: US-based internships are open to all students and recent graduates, but US-based interns must have work authorisation for the internship (the page notes that US-based international students typically have it). Each posting says whether remote candidates are accepted or whether it is limited to the DC area. Overseas centers have their own rules.
how_to_apply: Browse openings on carnegieendowment.applicantpro.com/jobs
Check the posting for location, remote option and dates
Apply online with CV and cover letter
carnegie-endowment-internships.costs: At least USD 20 per hour for all US-based interns; full-time interns receive benefits.

cern-technical-student-programme.about:
Technical Studentships at CERN let students work for 4 to 12 months in a technical team, applying their studies to accelerator, detector, IT or engineering projects. Students stay full-time students of their home university during the placement.

Vacancies are advertised individually on the CERN careers site with their own deadlines. A CV in English or French is the main requirement; a reference letter and transcript are optional. Selected candidates are interviewed online.

This is separate from the CERN Summer Student Programme (already listed on Meridian).
cern-technical-student-programme.eligibility: National of a CERN Member or Associate Member State (applicants from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Türkiye cannot currently be considered because the associate quota is full). At least three semesters of study in the field, full-time student for the whole placement, good English or French. PhD students and PhD holders are not eligible. Check the CERN member-state list for Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Check your nationality against the CERN member and associate member list
Watch the CERN careers portal for Technical Studentship vacancies
Submit your CV in English or French (reference letter and transcript optional)
Attend an online interview if selected
Accept the offer and arrange relocation to Geneva
cern-technical-student-programme.costs: No fee. CHF 3,486 net monthly allowance, 30 days paid leave per year; family supplement and travel to Geneva may apply.

ciee-college-first-year-abroad.about:
CIEE describes College First Year Abroad as 1-2 semesters of college abroad for recent high-school graduates, designed to keep students on track to graduate in four years. It is one of the programme tracks on the CIEE high-school study abroad page and is applied for through MyCIEE.

Costs, destinations and deadlines are not published on that page; contact CIEE.
ciee-college-first-year-abroad.eligibility: Aimed at high-school students and recent graduates, mostly U.S.-based. Check CIEE for the citizenship and residency rules of each programme.
how_to_apply: Open the CIEE high school study abroad page and choose a programme.
Apply through MyCIEE (my.ciee.org).
Ask about scholarship funds: CIEE says it administers a large fund for U.S. high-school students.
ciee-college-first-year-abroad.costs: Costs and deadlines are not stated on the programme page; CIEE says it awards roughly USD 6-7 million a year in scholarships to U.S. high-school students.

ciee-gap-year-abroad.about:
The CIEE high-school study abroad page lists Gap Year Abroad for recent high-school graduates, lasting one or two semesters. It is applied for through the MyCIEE portal and is part of CIEE's study abroad range with scholarship funds mainly for U.S. students.

The page does not state costs, deadlines or destinations for the gap-year track; ask CIEE (hsabroad@ciee.org, 866-583-0332).
ciee-gap-year-abroad.eligibility: Aimed at high-school students and recent graduates, mostly U.S.-based. Check CIEE for the citizenship and residency rules of each programme.
how_to_apply: Open the CIEE high school study abroad page and choose a programme.
Apply through MyCIEE (my.ciee.org).
Ask about scholarship funds: CIEE says it administers a large fund for U.S. high-school students.
ciee-gap-year-abroad.costs: Costs and deadlines are not stated on the programme page; CIEE says it awards roughly USD 6-7 million a year in scholarships to U.S. high-school students.

ciee-high-school-study-abroad-semester-y.about:
CIEE has run study abroad programmes since 1947 and supports more than 3,500 U.S. high-school students abroad each year. The semester and academic-year programmes place students in a local high school; destinations named on the page include Spain, Japan and France.

Students are mostly juniors and seniors, though about 20% are rising sophomores. Apply through the MyCIEE portal; CIEE administers a large scholarship fund.
ciee-high-school-study-abroad-semester-y.eligibility: Aimed at high-school students and recent graduates, mostly U.S.-based. Check CIEE for the citizenship and residency rules of each programme.
how_to_apply: Open the CIEE high school study abroad page and choose a programme.
Apply through MyCIEE (my.ciee.org).
Ask about scholarship funds: CIEE says it administers a large fund for U.S. high-school students.
ciee-high-school-study-abroad-semester-y.costs: Costs and deadlines are not stated on the programme page; CIEE says it awards roughly USD 6-7 million a year in scholarships to U.S. high-school students.

cjeu-traineeships-2027-2028.about:
The Court offers two sessions a year (1 March to 31 July, and 1 October to end of February) in the Chambers of Judges and Advocates General, and in 13 administrative departments including Legal Translation. There are also a disability programme and a place for national judges through the EJTN.

Trainees are paid about EUR 2,400 a month. Admission gives no right to later recruitment.
cjeu-traineeships-2027-2028.eligibility: EU Member State nationals (exceptions possible in justified cases). University degree in any field (for Chambers: law, political science, economics or related). Thorough knowledge of one official EU language and good knowledge of another; good French or English. No prior paid or unpaid post or traineeship of over six weeks in an EU institution or body.
how_to_apply: Check the open session on the Court's traineeships page
Apply online via EU CV Online during the application window
Disability applicants choose a field and provide documentation
Successful applicants are contacted by the Court's HR department
cjeu-traineeships-2027-2028.costs: Monthly grant of about EUR 2,400; possible one-off travel allowance of EUR 150. No fees.

cor-cicero-traineeship-2027.about:
The Cicero traineeship lasts five months with two sessions a year: spring (16 February to 15 July) and autumn (16 September to 15 February). Candidates choose up to three CoR departments in an online form.

Trainees receive about EUR 1,538 a month plus a travel and mobility allowance.
cor-cicero-traineeship-2027.eligibility: EU citizens. Non-EU citizens, including UK citizens, can apply but are selected only in exceptional cases (candidacy of particular interest to the CoR and the right to reside and work in Belgium). Full undergraduate degree or at least three years of higher education by the deadline. Fluency in one EU language and satisfactory English or French. Not accepted: more than 8 weeks of in-house placement at, or any employment in, a European institution or body.
how_to_apply: Choose up to three CoR departments
Complete the online form at candform.cor.europa.eu before the session deadline (noon Brussels time)
One application per traineeship period; late or non-electronic applications are refused
cor-cicero-traineeship-2027.costs: Monthly grant about EUR 1,538 with travel and mobility allowance; accident insurance covered, health insurance optional.

council-of-europe-traineeships.about:
The Council of Europe (46 member states, the home of the European Convention on Human Rights) takes trainees for about six months, mostly in Strasbourg, in departments covering human rights, democracy, rule of law, culture, education and administration. The European Court of Human Rights recruits law graduates in the same scheme (some departments accept applicants who have finished the first year of a master's).

Trainees receive about EUR 1,320 gross a month and health insurance. The annual call is advertised on the Jobs and Traineeships page; the 2026-27 call closed in June 2026, and the next is expected around the same time in 2027. Separate study visits to the Court (three to eight weeks) are arranged directly with it.
council-of-europe-traineeships.eligibility: At least 18; citizen of a Council of Europe member state (Georgia is a member; Qatar is not eligible); bachelor degree or equivalent with at least three years of university study before the deadline; very good English or French. No previous CoE traineeship or employment; no close relatives on staff.
how_to_apply: Watch the Council of Europe Jobs and Traineeships page for the annual call.
Choose departments and complete the online application.
Upload degree, CV and motivation letter.
Interviews and selection follow; sessions start in autumn.
council-of-europe-traineeships.costs: About EUR 1,320 gross monthly grant in Strasbourg plus health insurance. No fee.

council-of-the-eu-traineeships.about:
The Council of the EU, where member-state ministers negotiate EU law, hosts trainees in its General Secretariat in Brussels for two five-month periods a year (1 February to 30 June and 1 September to 31 January). Trainees work in policy, legal, communication, translation and administrative units.

The grant is EUR 1,538.16 net per month, plus a EUR 70 meal allowance and a travel allowance (capped at EUR 800) for trainees recruited from more than 50 km away. Up to six places a year are reserved for EU nationals with a recognised disability, who may receive up to 50% extra.

The next application window opens on 8 February 2027 for the September 2027 to January 2028 period.
council-of-the-eu-traineeships.eligibility: Holder of at least a bachelor-level diploma by the closing date. Open mainly to EU citizens; a limited number of places for non-EU nationals may be offered (check the page). Knowledge of two EU languages (one of them English or French is typical). Georgian and Qatari citizens are generally not eligible unless the page lists non-EU places.
how_to_apply: Wait for the application window (opens 8 February 2027).
Create an account and complete the online form.
Upload degree, CV and motivation.
Selection runs for several months before the start date.
council-of-the-eu-traineeships.costs: Grant EUR 1,538.16 net/month, EUR 70/month meals, travel allowance up to EUR 800. No fee.

crick-summer-student-training-programme.about:
The Crick's Summer Student Training Programme pairs undergraduates with postdoctoral supervisors in a research group for nine weeks. Students receive funding at the London Living Wage level and present their results at a student symposium; a small cohort (around twenty) is accepted.

The 2026 call targeted motivated second-year undergraduates at UK universities, with a February deadline and interviews in late March. The Crick also runs a separate 12-month sandwich placement.

Because only the 2026 call has been seen, confirm the 2027 eligibility and dates on the Crick page when the call opens.
crick-summer-student-training-programme.eligibility: In the 2026 call: second-year undergraduates at UK universities. International students who are enrolled at a UK university and have the right to work in the UK may be considered; students at universities outside the UK should not assume eligibility and should confirm with the Crick.
how_to_apply: Watch the Crick summer student page for the 2027 call (the 2026 call opened in late 2025)
Prepare a CV and personal statement and arrange an academic reference
Apply online before the closing date (early February in 2026)
Attend an interview (late March in 2026)
Complete the nine weeks and present at the symposium
crick-summer-student-training-programme.costs: No fee. Paid at London Living Wage level for the nine weeks.

csis-internship-program.about:
About 200 interns a year support CSIS programmes and departments through research, writing and project development, and take part in the Abshire-Inamori Leadership Academy (AILA) programming on leadership, ethics and foreign policy.

Internships run in fall, spring and summer for undergraduates, graduate students and recent graduates; applications are made through the Internship Opportunities link on the CSIS Careers page.
csis-internship-program.eligibility: Undergraduate students, graduate students and recent graduates. The page says nothing about pay, nationality or US work authorisation; confirm with CSIS HR (Contact HR page) before applying from abroad.
how_to_apply: Open the CSIS internships page
Use the Internship Opportunities link to the careers application section
Apply to the posting for your term
csis-internship-program.costs: Pay is not stated on the page.

ctbto-internship-programme.about:
The CTBTO monitors the globe for nuclear explosions, and interns support its Vienna-based divisions on seismic and radionuclide data, IT, legal, public information and international cooperation.

Interns are 18 to 35 with at least two years of university study or up to two years after a degree, fluent in English. A EUR 500 monthly stipend may be provided where funds allow and the intern has no other support. Interns pay for travel, living costs and medical coverage.
ctbto-internship-programme.eligibility: Age 18 to 35; at least two years of full-time university study; may apply up to two years after a bachelor, master or doctorate; excellent English. Open to all nationalities (check the vacancy).
how_to_apply: Check internship vacancies on the CTBTO employment page.
Apply online with CV and motivation.
If selected, arrange travel, visa and medical cover.
ctbto-internship-programme.costs: EUR 500/month possible; travel, living and medical costs at intern's expense.

deutsche-bank-dbacademy-asia-pacific.about: Applicants complete a behavioural and aptitude test followed by a short video interview.
deutsche-bank-dbacademy-asia-pacific.eligibility: University students in early years; right to work in the region; English.
how_to_apply: Open the programme page.
Complete behavioural and aptitude test.
Short video interview.
Attend.
